newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Lee Kuan Yew in hospital for tests.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Lee Kuan Yew in hospital for tests.

text.p: Singapore patriarch Lee Kuan Yew was in hospital on Saturday for scheduled tests on his bladder, a statement from the office of Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said.

The statement said Lee, 73, who led Singapore for 31 years until 1990 and remains in the cabinet as Senior Minister, had had chronic inflammatory tissue removed from the wall of his bladder on two previous occasions.
"His stay in hospital will depend upon the extent of the operation," it said.
It gave no other details of Lee's condition.
A doctor contacted by Reuters said inflammation of the bladder was a fairly common condition and was usually caused by an infection.
"The idea of the tests may be to make sure there's nothing more serious -- to make sure it is not cancerous," said the doctor, who declined to be identified.
Lee, who retains considerable influence in Singapore, had two heart operations in early 1996, raising fears of a drop on financial markets in the prosperous city-state.
But the markets took news of his condition in their stride, a reaction which Lee said afterwards proved Singapore had accepted that the reins of power had passed to a new generation.
